Following up on the SAT participation review: among the currently operating high schools in the district with NCES identification number 0613360 that had no SAT test takers, which one begins serving students at the earliest grade? Please give me each such school's name and grade span served. Note that a high school must actually enroll students through grade 12-offering grade 12 without enrollment doesn't count. A school with no SAT record counts as having zero SAT test takers and should be included; only exclude schools with a positive number of SAT test takers. Compare starting grades as school grades-preschool comes before kindergarten, which comes before grade 1-and use the lowest grade the school actually serves, not just what it offers. If several schools tie at the earliest grade, list them all alphabetically by school name.

No follow-up user is available. Give the best supported answer for the question. Return your final answer as exactly one fenced SQL block containing a single read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH query. Exclude intermediate SQL.

calls.content:
```sql
WITH hs_in_district AS (
  SELECT
    s.school_id,
    s.school_name,
    s.nces_district_id,
    s.operational_status,
    s.low_grade_served,
    s.high_grade_served,
    s.grade12_enrollment
  FROM schools s
  WHERE s.nces_district_id = '0613360'
    AND s.operational_status = 'Currently Operational'
    AND s.high_grade_served = '12'
    AND IFNULL(s.grade12_enrollment, 0) > 0
),
sat_takers_by_school AS (
  SELECT
    sc.school_id,
    SUM(COALESCE(ss.num_test_takers, 0)) AS total_sat_takers
  FROM hs_in_district sc
  LEFT JOIN satscores ss ON sc.school_id = ss.school_id
  GROUP BY sc.school_id
),
eligible_schools AS (
  SELECT
    sc.school_id,
    sc.school_name,
    sc.low_grade_served,
    sc.high_grade_served
  FROM hs_in_district sc
  INNER JOIN sat_takers_by_school st ON sc.school_id = st.school_id
  WHERE st.total_sat_takers = 0
),
ranked_schools AS (
  SELECT
    es.school_id,
    es.school_name,
    es.low_grade_served,
    es.high_grade_served,
    CASE
      WHEN es.low_grade_served = 'PK' THEN 0
      WHEN es.low_grade_served = 'KG' THEN 1
      WHEN CAST(es.low_grade_served AS INTEGER) = 1 THEN 2
      WHEN CAST(es.low_grade_served AS INTEGER) > 1 THEN 1 + CAST(es.low_grade_served AS INTEGER)
      ELSE 100
    END AS sort_grade
  FROM eligible_schools es
)
SELECT
  school_name,
  low_grade_served AS starting_grade,
  high_grade_served AS ending_grade
FROM ranked_schools
WHERE sort_grade = (SELECT MIN(sort_grade) FROM ranked_schools)
ORDER BY school_name;
```

What was the average number of SAT test takers per school across Los Angeles County schools that opened during 2007 and are run by a school district? Please give me that single number, rounded to two decimals. A few things to keep in mind: a county office of education counts as the school district for the schools it runs; "opened during 2007" means the opening date falls in calendar year 2007; and a school with no SAT record counts as zero test takers.

    SELECT

            END

            CASE
                WHEN s.AvgScrRead IS NOT NULL AND s.AvgScrMath IS NOT NULL AND s.AvgScrWrite IS NOT NULL

WITH active_charters AS (

first_request.user:
Among California's state special schools, which one begins enrolling students at the latest grade level? Please give me: the school's name, the earliest grade level covered by its K-12 enrollment, its K-12 enrollment, and how many SAT test takers it had. In the grade-level codes, P means pre-kindergarten and K means kindergarten, and grades progress from pre-kindergarten to kindergarten to grades 1 through 12 — so a school starting at grade 1 starts later than one starting at kindergarten. If a state special school has no SAT record, still consider it a candidate and report it as having 0 SAT test takers. If two schools start at the same grade level, prefer the one with the larger K-12 enrollment; if still tied, the one whose name comes first alphabetically. The data is for the 2014-2015 school year.

No follow-up user is available. Give the best supported answer for the question. Return your final answer as exactly one fenced SQL block containing a single read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH query. Exclude intermediate SQL.

```sql
WITH cal_state_special AS (
  SELECT
    s.name,
    s.cdscode,
    s.gslo,
    s.enr_k12
  FROM schools s
  WHERE
    s.stype = 'Special' AND
    s.agency_type = 'State' AND
    s.fy = 2015 AND
    s.st = 'CA'
),
grade_order AS (
  -- Assign progressive order to grade-level codes: P < K < 1 < 2 ... < 12
  SELECT 'P' AS gslo, 0 AS gslo_order UNION ALL
  SELECT 'K', 1 UNION ALL
  SELECT '1', 2 UNION ALL SELECT '2', 3 UNION ALL
  SELECT '3', 4 UNION ALL SELECT '4', 5 UNION ALL
  SELECT '5', 6 UNION ALL SELECT '6', 7 UNION ALL
  SELECT '7', 8 UNION ALL SELECT '8', 9 UNION ALL
  SELECT '9', 10 UNION ALL SELECT '10', 11 UNION ALL
  SELECT '11', 12 UNION ALL SELECT '12', 13
),
with_sat AS (
  SELECT
    c.name,
    c.gslo,
    c.enr_k12,
    COALESCE(SUM(s.satnum),0) AS sat_test_takers,
    g.gslo_order
  FROM cal_state_special c
  JOIN grade_order g ON c.gslo = g.gslo
  LEFT JOIN satscores s
    ON c.cdscode = s.cdscode AND s.fy = 2015
  GROUP BY c.name, c.gslo, c.enr_k12, g.gslo_order
)
SELECT
  name AS school_name,
  gslo AS earliest_grade_level,
  enr_k12 AS k12_enrollment,
  sat_test_takers
FROM with_sat
ORDER BY gslo_order DESC, k12_enrollment DESC, name ASC
LIMIT 1;

FROM joined
WHERE StatusType = 'Active'
GROUP BY [Charter Funding Type]
ORDER BY CASE [Charter Funding Type] WHEN 'Directly Funded' THEN 1 WHEN 'Locally Funded' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END;

WITH charter_schools_by_county_office AS (
  SELECT
    sch.school_id,
    sch.charter_funding_type,

    sch.status
  FROM schools sch
  JOIN frpm ON sch.school_id = frpm.school_id

    AND sch.operated_by_type = 'County Office of Education'
    AND sch.charter_funding_type IN ('Directly Funded', 'Locally Funded')

ORDER BY
  CASE
    WHEN charter_funding_type = 'Directly Funded' THEN 1
    WHEN charter_funding_type = 'Locally Funded' THEN 2
    ELSE 3
  END
;

The county I mean is the one where Fremont High (CDS code 1612590125716) is located - please identify the county by that CDS code, not by the school name. For that county, please look at all K-12 schools with more than 500 free meals and fewer than 700 FRPM meals, and give me back: the county name; the number of schools; the average free-meal percentage and the average FRPM percentage, both on a 0-100 scale with each school's own percentage rounded to 2 decimals before averaging; the number of charter schools and the number of non-charter schools (charter vs. non-charter per the charter indicator in the frpm data); and the average SAT score, where a school's SAT score is the sum of its three SAT section averages, counted only for schools that actually have SAT records, with no SAT record meaning the school is simply excluded from that average. Please round the reported averages to 2 decimals.

WITH fremont_county AS (
  SELECT county_name 
  FROM schools 
  WHERE cds = '1612590125716'
  LIMIT 1
),
target_schools AS (
  SELECT 
    s.cds,
    s.schoolname,
    s.county_name,
    f.total_meals_free,
    f.total_meals_frpm,
    ROUND(100.0 * f.percent_meals_free, 2) AS pct_free,
    ROUND(100.0 * f.percent_meals_frpm, 2) AS pct_frpm,
    f.charter_indicator
  FROM frpm f

  CROSS JOIN fremont_county fc
  WHERE

    AND f.total_meals_free > 500
    AND f.total_meals_frpm < 700
),

  SELECT
    county_name,

    ROUND(AVG(pct_free), 2) AS avg_free_pct,

    SUM(CASE WHEN charter_indicator = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS num_charter,
    SUM(CASE WHEN charter_indicator = 'N' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS num_non_charter
  FROM target_schools
),
school_sat AS (
  SELECT 
    t.cds,
    (s.sat_evidence_based_reading_writing_avg + s.sat_math_avg + s.sat_essay_avg) AS school_sat_total

  r.num_charter,

  a.avg_sat_total
FROM rounded_avgs r
CROSS JOIN avg_sat a;

sql:
WITH eligible_schools AS (
  SELECT
    s.CDSCode,
    s.School AS school_name,
    s.GSserved,
    s.Charter,
    f.[Percent (%) Eligible Free (K-12)] AS free_meal_rate
  FROM schools s
  JOIN frpm f ON s.CDSCode = f.CDSCode
  WHERE s.County = 'Alameda'
    AND s.GSserved LIKE '%12'
    AND s.GSserved IS NOT NULL
    AND f.[Percent (%) Eligible Free (K-12)] IS NOT NULL
),
max_frpm AS (
  SELECT MAX(free_meal_rate) AS max_rate FROM eligible_schools
),
tied_schools AS (
  SELECT
    es.CDSCode,
    es.school_name,
    ROUND(es.free_meal_rate, 4) AS free_meal_rate,
    CASE es.Charter WHEN 1 THEN 'Yes' WHEN 0 THEN 'No' ELSE 'Unknown' END AS is_charter_school,
    es.GSserved AS grades_served
  FROM eligible_schools es
  JOIN max_frpm m ON es.free_meal_rate = m.max_rate
)
SELECT
  t.school_name,
  t.free_meal_rate,
  t.is_charter_school,
  t.grades_served,
  CASE 
    WHEN ss.AvgScrRead IS NULL AND ss.AvgScrMath IS NULL AND ss.AvgScrWrite IS NULL THEN 'No SAT Data'
    ELSE CASE 
      WHEN (IFNULL(ss.AvgScrRead,0) + IFNULL(ss.AvgScrMath,0) + IFNULL(ss.AvgScrWrite,0))/3.0 < 
        (SELECT AVG(totalavg) FROM (SELECT (IFNULL(AvgScrRead,0)+IFNULL(AvgScrMath,0)+IFNULL(AvgScrWrite,0))/3.0 AS totalavg FROM satscores WHERE AvgScrRead IS NOT NULL OR AvgScrMath IS NOT NULL OR AvgScrWrite IS NOT NULL)) THEN 'Below Average'
      WHEN (IFNULL(ss.AvgScrRead,0) + IFNULL(ss.AvgScrMath,0) + IFNULL(ss.AvgScrWrite,0))/3.0 > 
        (SELECT AVG(totalavg) FROM (SELECT (IFNULL(AvgScrRead,0)+IFNULL(AvgScrMath,0)+IFNULL(AvgScrWrite,0))/3.0 AS totalavg FROM satscores WHERE AvgScrRead IS NOT NULL OR AvgScrMath IS NOT NULL OR AvgScrWrite IS NOT NULL)) THEN 'Above Average'
      ELSE 'Average'
    END
  END AS sat_performance
FROM tied_schools t
LEFT JOIN satscores ss ON t.CDSCode = ss.cds
GROUP BY t.CDSCode, t.school_name, t.free_meal_rate, t.is_charter_school, t.grades_served

LIMIT 1000

  FROM schools s
  JOIN frpm f ON s.school_code = f.school_code
  WHERE s.county_name = 'Alameda'
    AND s.GSserved LIKE '%12'
    AND s.GSserved NOT IN ('UG') -- Exclude "ungraded" if present

WITH exclusively_virtual_schools AS (
  SELECT
    County,
    School,
    CDSCode
  FROM schools
  WHERE LOWER(Virtual) = 'exclusively virtual'
),
county_virtual_counts AS (
  SELECT
    County,
    COUNT(*) AS exclusively_virtual_count
  FROM exclusively_virtual_schools
  GROUP BY County
),
limits AS (
  SELECT exclusively_virtual_count
  FROM county_virtual_counts
  ORDER BY exclusively_virtual_count DESC
  LIMIT 5
),
threshold AS (
  SELECT MIN(exclusively_virtual_count) AS cutoff
  FROM limits
),
top_counties AS (
  SELECT cvc.County, cvc.exclusively_virtual_count
  FROM county_virtual_counts cvc
  CROSS JOIN threshold t
  WHERE cvc.exclusively_virtual_count >= t.cutoff
),
school_with_scores AS (
  SELECT
    evs.County,
    evs.School,
    evs.CDSCode,
    ss.AvgScrRead
  FROM exclusively_virtual_schools evs
  LEFT JOIN satscores ss
    ON evs.CDSCode = ss.cds AND ss.rtype = 'S'
),
ranked_schools AS (
  SELECT
    sws.County,
    sws.School,
    sws.AvgScrRead,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sws.County ORDER BY sws.AvgScrRead DESC)
      AS reading_rank
  FROM school_with_scores sws
  WHERE sws.County IN (SELECT County FROM top_counties)
),
top_school_in_county AS (
  SELECT
    County,
    GROUP_CONCAT(School, ', ') AS top_school_name
  FROM ranked_schools
  WHERE reading_rank = 1 AND AvgScrRead IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY County
),
counties_with_score AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT County FROM top_school_in_county
),
counties_no_reported_scores AS (
  SELECT tc.County
  FROM top_counties tc
  LEFT JOIN counties_with_score cws ON tc.County = cws.County
  WHERE cws.County IS NULL
)
SELECT
  tc.County,
  tc.exclusively_virtual_count,
  COALESCE(tsic.top_school_name, 'None') AS top_school_name
FROM top_counties tc
LEFT JOIN top_school_in_county tsic ON tc.County = tsic.County
ORDER BY tc.exclusively_virtual_count DESC, tc.County;

calls.content:
```sql
WITH exclusively_virtual_schools AS (
  SELECT
    s.school_id,
    s.name AS school_name,
    s.county,
    s.is_exclusively_virtual
  FROM schools s
  WHERE s.is_exclusively_virtual = 1
),
county_virtual_counts AS (
  SELECT
    evs.county,
    COUNT(evs.school_id) AS virtual_school_count
  FROM exclusively_virtual_schools evs
  GROUP BY evs.county
),
top_counts AS (
  SELECT
    cvc.county,
    cvc.virtual_school_count,
    RANK() OVER (ORDER BY cvc.virtual_school_count DESC) AS rnk
  FROM county_virtual_counts cvc
),
top5_counts AS (
  SELECT
    county,
    virtual_school_count
  FROM top_counts
  WHERE virtual_school_count >= (
    SELECT MIN(virtual_school_count)
    FROM (
      SELECT virtual_school_count
      FROM county_virtual_counts
      ORDER BY virtual_school_count DESC
      LIMIT 5
    )
  )
),
county_virtual_sat AS (
  SELECT
    evs.county,
    evs.school_id,
    evs.school_name,
    COALESCE(sc.reading_avg, NULL) AS reading_avg
  FROM exclusively_virtual_schools evs
  LEFT JOIN satscores sc
    ON evs.school_id = sc.school_id
),
county_top_school AS (
  SELECT
    tvc.county,
    cvsat.school_id,
    cvsat.school_name,
    cvsat.reading_avg,
    RANK() OVER (
      PARTITION BY tvc.county
      ORDER BY cvsat.reading_avg DESC
    ) AS reading_rank
  FROM top5_counts tvc
  JOIN county_virtual_sat cvsat ON tvc.county = cvsat.county
)
SELECT
  ct.county,
  ct.virtual_school_count,
  COALESCE(cts.school_name, 'None') AS top_school_name,
  cts.reading_avg AS top_school_reading_avg
FROM
  top5_counts ct
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    county,
    school_name,
    reading_avg
  FROM county_top_school
  WHERE (reading_rank = 1 AND reading_avg IS NOT NULL)
  UNION ALL
  -- If none in the county has reading_avg, show just one 'None'
  SELECT
    cvs.county,
    NULL AS school_name,
    NULL AS reading_avg
  FROM (
    SELECT county
    FROM top5_counts
  ) cvs
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM county_top_school cts WHERE cts.county = cvs.county AND cts.reading_avg IS NOT NULL
  )
) cts
ON ct.county = cts.county
ORDER BY ct.virtual_school_count DESC, ct.county, cts.top_school_name
```

sql:
WITH eligible_schools AS (
  SELECT
    s.CDSCode AS cdscode,
    s.School AS school_name,
    s.County,
    s.City,
    s.MailStreet,
    s.MailCity,
    s.MailState,
    s.MailZip,
    s.Website,
    f."Enrollment (K-12)" AS k12enroll,
    f."FRPM Count (K-12)" AS frpm_num_eligible,
    CASE WHEN f."Enrollment (K-12)" != 0 THEN f."FRPM Count (K-12)"/f."Enrollment (K-12)" ELSE NULL END AS frpm_share,
    s.OpenDate,
    s.ClosedDate,
    CASE WHEN s.ClosedDate IS NULL THEN 'open' ELSE 'closed' END AS status
  FROM schools s
  JOIN frpm f ON s.CDSCode = f.CDSCode
  WHERE
    f."School Type" = 'Regular'
    AND (f."Charter School (Y/N)" IS NULL OR f."Charter School (Y/N)" = 0)
    AND f."Enrollment (K-12)" > 100
),
sat_joined AS (
  SELECT
    e.*,
    sat.NumTstTakr,
    sat.NumGE1500,
    sat.AvgScrRead,
    sat.AvgScrMath,
    sat.AvgScrWrite,
    (CAST(sat.AvgScrRead AS FLOAT) + CAST(sat.AvgScrMath AS FLOAT) + CAST(sat.AvgScrWrite AS FLOAT)) AS avg_total_sat,

FROM qualifying_schools
GROUP BY county
ORDER BY num_qualifying_schools DESC, county ASC;

Please list only counties that have at least one such school, with the county name and the number of its qualifying schools, sorted from most such schools to fewest, and alphabetically by county name when counties tie.

WITH qualifying_schools AS (
  SELECT
    s.county,
    s.id AS school_id
  FROM
    schools s
    JOIN satscores sat ON s.id = sat.school_id
  WHERE
    s.year = '2014-15'
    AND s.frpm_eligible_rate > 0.1
    AND sat.sat_total >= 1500
)
SELECT

  SELECT
    cs.CDSCode,
    cs.AdmFName1,
    cs.AdmLName1,

FROM joined
WHERE sat_1500plus = (SELECT MAX(sat_1500plus) FROM joined)
ORDER BY CDSCode ASC
LIMIT 1;

WITH variable_power_cards AS (
  SELECT uuid
  FROM cards
  WHERE power IS NULL OR power LIKE '%{%'
),
cards_with_triggered_ruling AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT r.uuid
  FROM rulings r
  WHERE r.text LIKE '%triggered ability%'
)
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.uuid) AS num_distinct_card_printings

WITH set_types AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT type AS set_type FROM sets
),
translated_sets AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT s.code AS set_code, s.type AS set_type
  FROM sets s
  INNER JOIN set_translations st ON s.code = st.setCode
),
cards_in_translated_sets AS (
  SELECT ts.set_type, COUNT(c.id) AS total_cards
  FROM translated_sets ts
  JOIN cards c ON c.setCode = ts.set_code
  GROUP BY ts.set_type
),
set_count_with_translation AS (
  SELECT set_type, COUNT(DISTINCT set_code) AS set_count
  FROM translated_sets
  GROUP BY set_type
)
SELECT
  st.set_type,
  COALESCE(sct.set_count, 0) AS sets_with_official_translation,
  COALESCE(cts.total_cards, 0) AS total_cards_in_translated_sets
FROM set_types st
LEFT JOIN set_count_with_translation sct ON st.set_type = sct.set_type
LEFT JOIN cards_in_translated_sets cts ON st.set_type = cts.set_type
ORDER BY st.set_type ASC;

    c.id,
    c.frame,
    c.set_code
  FROM cards c
  WHERE LOWER(c.name) = 'tarmogoyf'
),
frame_counts AS (
  SELECT
    frame,
    COUNT(*) AS count
  FROM tarmogoyf_cards
  GROUP BY frame
),
latest_frame AS (
  SELECT

  FROM frame_counts
  WHERE frame IS NOT NULL
  ORDER BY frame DESC

FROM latest_frame_count l

sql:
WITH
-- 1. Find all sets containing 'Abyssal Horror'
ah_sets AS (
  SELECT c.setCode
  FROM cards c
  WHERE c.name = 'Abyssal Horror'
),
-- 2. Get release dates for those sets
ah_set_dates AS (
  SELECT s.code, s.releaseDate
  FROM sets s
  JOIN ah_sets a ON s.code = a.setCode
),
-- 3. Get the "first print" set: earliest date, tiebreak on set code
first_printed_set AS (
  SELECT code
  FROM ah_set_dates
  WHERE releaseDate = (SELECT MIN(releaseDate) FROM ah_set_dates)
  ORDER BY code
  LIMIT 1
),
-- 4. Get the most recent set (latest date, tiebreak on code)
recent_set AS (
  SELECT code
  FROM sets
  WHERE releaseDate = (SELECT MAX(releaseDate) FROM sets)
  ORDER BY code
  LIMIT 1
),
-- 5. Pick both set codes
target_sets AS (
  SELECT code FROM first_printed_set
  UNION ALL
  SELECT code FROM recent_set
),
-- 6. Get set names
target_set_names AS (
  SELECT ts.code, s.name
  FROM target_sets ts
  JOIN sets s ON ts.code = s.code
),
-- 7. For each target set, count #cards with manaCost (not null/blank) and # of those with convertedManaCost <= 3
set_mana_stats AS (
  SELECT
    tsn.name AS set_name,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN c.manaCost IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(c.manaCost) <> '' THEN 1 END) AS cards_with_mana_cost,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN c.manaCost IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(c.manaCost) <> '' AND c.convertedManaCost <= 3 THEN 1 END) AS cheap_cards
  FROM target_set_names tsn
  JOIN cards c ON c.setCode = tsn.code
  GROUP BY tsn.name
)
SELECT
  set_name,
  ROUND(
    CAST(cheap_cards AS REAL) * 100.0 / NULLIF(cards_with_mana_cost, 0)
  , 2) AS percent_cheap_cards
FROM set_mana_stats;

By "first printed", I mean the set with the earliest release date among the sets Abyssal Horror appears in; if several share that earliest date, use the one whose set code comes first alphabetically. For the most recent set, use the latest release date among all sets; if several share that date, again take the one whose set code comes first alphabetically. By "converted mana cost" I mean the card's mana value, and a card counts as having a mana cost only if a mana cost is printed on it.

No follow-up user is available. Give the best supported answer for the question. Return your final answer as exactly one fenced SQL block containing a single read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH query. Exclude intermediate SQL.

calls.content:
```sql
WITH
-- 1. Find all sets containing 'Abyssal Horror'
ah_sets AS (
  SELECT c.set_code
  FROM cards c
  WHERE c.name = 'Abyssal Horror'
),
-- 2. Get release dates for those sets
ah_set_dates AS (
  SELECT s.code, s.release_date
  FROM sets s
  JOIN ah_sets a ON s.code = a.set_code
),
-- 3. Get the "first print" set: earliest date, tiebreak on set code
first_printed_set AS (
  SELECT code
  FROM ah_set_dates
  WHERE release_date = (SELECT MIN(release_date) FROM ah_set_dates)
  ORDER BY code
  LIMIT 1
),
-- 4. Get the most recent set (latest date, tiebreak on code)
recent_set AS (
  SELECT code
  FROM sets
  WHERE release_date = (SELECT MAX(release_date) FROM sets)
  ORDER BY code
  LIMIT 1
),
-- 5. Pick both set codes
target_sets AS (
  SELECT code FROM first_printed_set
  UNION ALL
  SELECT code FROM recent_set
),
-- 6. Get set names
target_set_names AS (
  SELECT ts.code, s.name
  FROM target_sets ts
  JOIN sets s ON ts.code = s.code
),
-- 7. For each target set, count #cards with mana_cost (not null/blank) and # of those with mana_value <= 3
set_mana_stats AS (
  SELECT
    tsn.name AS set_name,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN c.mana_cost IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(c.mana_cost) <> '' THEN 1 END) AS cards_with_mana_cost,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN c.mana_cost IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(c.mana_cost) <> '' AND c.mana_value <= 3 THEN 1 END) AS cheap_cards
  FROM target_set_names tsn
  JOIN cards c ON c.set_code = tsn.code
  GROUP BY tsn.name
)
SELECT
  set_name,
  ROUND(
    CAST(cheap_cards AS REAL) * 100.0 / NULLIF(cards_with_mana_cost, 0)
  , 2) AS percent_cheap_cards
FROM set_mana_stats;
```

WITH abzan_cards AS (
  SELECT
    uuid,
    name,
    setCode,
    number
  FROM cards
  WHERE watermark = 'Abzan'
),
max_collector_cards AS (
  SELECT
    setCode,
    MAX(CAST(number AS INTEGER)) AS max_collector_number
  FROM abzan_cards
  GROUP BY setCode
),
candidates AS (
  SELECT
    a.uuid,
    a.name,
    a.setCode,
    a.number
  FROM abzan_cards a
  INNER JOIN max_collector_cards m
    ON a.setCode = m.setCode
    AND CAST(a.number AS INTEGER) = m.max_collector_number
)
SELECT
  c.name,
  c.number AS collector_number,
  COUNT(f.id) AS foreign_language_printings
FROM candidates c
LEFT JOIN foreign_data f ON c.uuid = f.uuid
GROUP BY c.uuid, c.name, c.number
ORDER BY c.setCode, CAST(c.number AS INTEGER);

calls.content:
```sql
WITH abzan_cards AS (
  SELECT
    id,
    name,
    set,
    collector_number
  FROM cards
  WHERE watermark = 'Abzan'
),
max_collector_cards AS (
  SELECT
    set,
    MAX(CAST(collector_number AS INTEGER)) AS max_collector_number
  FROM abzan_cards
  GROUP BY set
),
candidates AS (
  SELECT
    a.id,
    a.name,
    a.set,
    a.collector_number
  FROM abzan_cards a
  INNER JOIN max_collector_cards m
    ON a.set = m.set
    AND CAST(a.collector_number AS INTEGER) = m.max_collector_number
)
SELECT
  c.name,
  c.collector_number,
  COUNT(f.language) AS foreign_printings
FROM candidates c
LEFT JOIN foreign_data f ON c.id = f.oracle_id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name, c.collector_number
ORDER BY c.set, CAST(c.collector_number AS INTEGER), c.name;
```

WITH latest_frame AS (
  SELECT MAX(frame_effects) AS latest_frame_effect
  FROM cards
  WHERE frame_effects IS NOT NULL
), latest_frame_year AS (

  WHERE frame IS NOT NULL AND frame GLOB '[0-9]*'

SELECT name

WITH jp_boros_printings AS (
  SELECT 
    c.scryfallOracleId AS oracle_id,
    st.translation AS jp_name,

  FROM cards c

  LEFT JOIN rulings r ON c2.uuid = r.uuid
  GROUP BY dc.oracle_id, dc.jp_name, dc.english_type
)
SELECT 
  jp_name AS "Japanese Card Name",
  english_type AS "English Card Type",
  ruling_count AS "Ruling Count"
FROM ruling_counts
ORDER BY jp_name, english_type

    FROM users
    WHERE Location LIKE '%Germany%'

    FROM posts_2012 p
    INNER JOIN ger_users u ON p.LastEditorUserId = u.user_id

SELECT

    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ger_editors) AS num_ger_editors,
    (SELECT SUM(Reputation) FROM ger_editors) AS ger_editors_total_reputation
;

WITH months AS (
  SELECT '2010-01' AS month UNION ALL SELECT '2010-02' UNION ALL SELECT '2010-03' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2010-04' UNION ALL SELECT '2010-05' UNION ALL SELECT '2010-06' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2010-07' UNION ALL SELECT '2010-08' UNION ALL SELECT '2010-09' UNION ALL
  SELECT '2010-10' UNION ALL SELECT '2010-11' UNION ALL SELECT '2010-12'
),
monthly_posts AS (
  SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', postLinks.CreationDate) AS month, postLinks.RelatedPostId AS post_id
  FROM postLinks
  WHERE postLinks.CreationDate >= '2010-01-01' AND postLinks.CreationDate < '2011-01-01'
),
qualified_posts AS (
  SELECT mp.month, mp.post_id
  FROM monthly_posts mp
  JOIN posts p ON mp.post_id = p.Id
  WHERE COALESCE(p.AnswerCount, 0) <= 2
)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(cnt), 2) as average
FROM (
  SELECT m.month, COUNT(DISTINCT qp.post_id) AS cnt
  FROM months m
  LEFT JOIN qualified_posts qp ON m.month = qp.month
  GROUP BY m.month
)

WITH fuel_ids AS (
  SELECT ProductID FROM products WHERE Description LIKE '%fuel%'
),
filtered_txn AS (
  SELECT 
    t.CustomerID,
    c.Currency,
    strftime('%Y-%m', t.Date) AS ym
  FROM transactions_1k t
  JOIN customers c ON t.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
  WHERE t.ProductID IN (SELECT ProductID FROM fuel_ids)
    AND t.Date >= '2013-01-01' AND t.Date < '2013-12-01'
),
active_custs AS (
  SELECT CustomerID, Currency, COUNT(DISTINCT ym) AS month_count
  FROM filtered_txn
  GROUP BY CustomerID, Currency
  HAVING month_count = 11
),
currency_totals AS (
  SELECT Currency, COUNT(DISTINCT CustomerID) AS cust_count
  FROM active_custs
  GROUP BY Currency
),
max_cte AS (
  SELECT MAX(cust_count) AS max_count FROM currency_totals
)
SELECT c.Currency, c.cust_count AS customer_count
FROM currency_totals c JOIN max_cte m ON c.cust_count = m.max_count

I'm preparing a loyalty review of our steadily active customers in 2013. For each currency, I'd like to know how many customers bought fuel in every month from January through November 2013, with both January and November included. Please give me the currency and that customer count. If several currencies tie, list them all – no ranking needed.

No follow-up user is available. Give the best supported answer for the question. Return your final answer as exactly one fenced SQL block containing a single read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH query. Exclude intermediate SQL.

calls.content:
```sql
WITH jan_to_nov_2013 AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    strftime('%Y-%m', transaction_date) AS ym,
    currency
  FROM transactions_1k
  WHERE transaction_date >= '2013-01-01'
    AND transaction_date < '2013-12-01'
),
customers_by_currency AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    currency,
    COUNT(DISTINCT ym) AS active_months
  FROM jan_to_nov_2013
  GROUP BY customer_id, currency
),
steady_customers AS (
  SELECT
    currency,
    COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS steady_count
  FROM customers_by_currency
  WHERE active_months = 11
  GROUP BY currency
),
max_count AS (
  SELECT MAX(steady_count) AS top_count FROM steady_customers
)
SELECT
  s.currency,
  s.steady_count AS customer_count
FROM steady_customers s
JOIN max_count m ON s.steady_count = m.top_count;

I'm putting together currency-specific pricing proposals and need a sense of typical quarterly fuel consumption. Among customers who have fuel consumption recorded in the second quarter of 2013 (April, May and June 2013), what is the average amount of fuel consumed over the whole quarter by an EUR-paying customer, and the same average for a CZK-paying customer? Please round both averages to two decimal places. By EUR-paying / CZK-paying I mean a customer whose account currency is EUR / CZK.

```sql
WITH q2_2013_transactions AS (
  SELECT
    t.customer_id,
    SUM(t.quantity) AS total_fuel_q2
  FROM
    transactions_1k t
  WHERE
    t.transaction_date >= '2013-04-01'
    AND t.transaction_date < '2013-07-01'
  GROUP BY
    t.customer_id
),
eur_customers AS (
  SELECT customer_id
  FROM customers
  WHERE currency = 'EUR'
),
czk_customers AS (
  SELECT customer_id
  FROM customers
  WHERE currency = 'CZK'
),
customers_with_q2_consumption AS (
  SELECT q.customer_id, q.total_fuel_q2
  FROM q2_2013_transactions q
)
SELECT
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN c.customer_id IS NOT NULL THEN q.total_fuel_q2 END), 2) AS avg_fuel_eur,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN cz.customer_id IS NOT NULL THEN q.total_fuel_q2 END), 2) AS avg_fuel_czk
FROM
  customers_with_q2_consumption q
  LEFT JOIN eur_customers c ON q.customer_id = c.customer_id
  LEFT JOIN czk_customers cz ON q.customer_id = cz.customer_id
WHERE
  (c.customer_id IS NOT NULL OR cz.customer_id IS NOT NULL)
;
```

    SELECT player_api_id
    FROM Player
    WHERE birthday >= '1991-01-01'

    SELECT DISTINCT pa.player_api_id
    FROM Player_Attributes pa
    JOIN young_players yp ON pa.player_api_id = yp.player_api_id
    WHERE pa.defensive_work_rate IS NOT NULL
),
high_defensive_workrate_players AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT pa.player_api_id
    FROM Player_Attributes pa
    JOIN young_players yp ON pa.player_api_id = yp.player_api_id
    WHERE pa.defensive_work_rate = 'high'
)
SELECT
    ROUND(
        (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM high_defensive_workrate_players) * 100.0
        /
        NULLIF((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM defensive_workrate_players), 0)
        , 2
    ) AS high_def_workrate_percentage;

sql:
WITH RiskyTeams AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT t.team_api_id, t.team_short_name
    FROM Team_Attributes ta
    JOIN Team t ON ta.team_api_id = t.team_api_id
    WHERE ta.chanceCreationPassingClass = 'Risky'
),
NameCounts AS (
    SELECT team_short_name, COUNT(DISTINCT team_api_id) AS club_count
    FROM RiskyTeams
    GROUP BY team_short_name
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT team_api_id) > 1
),
SnapshotRisk AS (
    SELECT
        t.team_short_name,
        ta.team_api_id,
        ta.chanceCreationPassing
    FROM Team_Attributes ta
    JOIN Team t ON ta.team_api_id = t.team_api_id
    JOIN NameCounts nc ON t.team_short_name = nc.team_short_name
    WHERE date(ta.date) <= '2014-09-19'
      AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM Team_Attributes ta2
          WHERE ta2.team_api_id = ta.team_api_id
            AND date(ta2.date) > date(ta.date)
            AND date(ta2.date) <= '2014-09-19'
      )
)
SELECT
    nc.team_short_name,
    nc.club_count,
    ROUND(AVG(sr.chanceCreationPassing*1.0), 1) AS avg_chanceCreationPassing
FROM NameCounts nc
JOIN SnapshotRisk sr ON nc.team_short_name = sr.team_short_name
GROUP BY nc.team_short_name, nc.club_count
ORDER BY avg_chanceCreationPassing DESC, nc.team_short_name ASC;

sql:
WITH FastBuildUp AS (
  SELECT 
    ta.team_api_id, 
    ta.date AS ta_date, 
    ta.buildUpPlaySpeedClass
  FROM Team_Attributes ta
  WHERE ta.buildUpPlaySpeedClass = 'Fast'
),
LastFastBuildUpPerMatch AS (
  SELECT 
    m.id AS match_id,
    m.home_team_api_id AS team_api_id,
    m.date AS match_date,
    MAX(fb.ta_date) AS last_fb_date
  FROM Match m
  JOIN FastBuildUp fb 
    ON fb.team_api_id = m.home_team_api_id
    AND fb.ta_date <= m.date
  GROUP BY m.id, m.home_team_api_id, m.date
),
QualifiedMatches AS (
  SELECT m.id AS match_id, m.home_team_api_id AS team_api_id
  FROM Match m
  JOIN LastFastBuildUpPerMatch lfb 
    ON m.id = lfb.match_id AND m.home_team_api_id = lfb.team_api_id
  JOIN FastBuildUp fb 
    ON fb.team_api_id = lfb.team_api_id AND fb.ta_date = lfb.last_fb_date
  WHERE m.home_team_goal - m.away_team_goal >= 3
),
ClubWins AS (
  SELECT 
    t.id AS team_id, 
    t.team_api_id, 
    t.team_long_name, 
    t.team_short_name, 
    COUNT(qm.match_id) AS num_big_fast_home_wins
  FROM Team t
  JOIN QualifiedMatches qm ON t.team_api_id = qm.team_api_id
  GROUP BY t.id, t.team_api_id, t.team_long_name, t.team_short_name
),
MaxWins AS (
  SELECT MAX(num_big_fast_home_wins) AS max_wins FROM ClubWins
)
SELECT 
  cw.team_long_name AS club_name,
  cw.team_short_name,
  cw.num_big_fast_home_wins
FROM ClubWins cw
JOIN MaxWins mw ON cw.num_big_fast_home_wins = mw.max_wins
ORDER BY cw.num_big_fast_home_wins DESC, cw.team_long_name
LIMIT 1000

first_request.user:
I'm studying squad physical profiles in Serie A. For the 2008/2009 season and the 2015/2016 season of the Italian league, I'd like to know how many players appeared in matches that season (i.e. were listed in a match's lineup, including players who appeared in both seasons), and the average height of those players in centimeters, rounded to two decimals. One row per season with the season label, the count of players, and their average height.

No follow-up user is available. Give the best supported answer for the question. Return your final answer as exactly one fenced SQL block containing a single read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH query. Exclude intermediate SQL.

calls.content:
```sql
WITH italian_league_ids AS (
    SELECT id
    FROM League
    WHERE name = 'Italy Serie A'
),
target_seasons AS (
    SELECT '2008/2009' AS season_label, '2008-2009' AS season_str
    UNION ALL
    SELECT '2015/2016', '2015-2016'
),
serie_a_matches AS (
    SELECT m.id AS match_id, m.season
    FROM Match m
    JOIN italian_league_ids l ON m.league_id = l.id
    WHERE m.season IN ('2008-2009', '2015-2016')
),
match_players AS (
    SELECT
        m.season,
        p.id AS player_id
    FROM serie_a_matches m
    -- Each match has, in columns home_player_X and away_player_X, the player IDs
    -- We'll use UNNEST-like logic by unioning all slots
    JOIN Player p
    WHERE p.id IN (
        m.home_player_1, m.home_player_2, m.home_player_3, m.home_player_4, m.home_player_5,
        m.home_player_6, m.home_player_7, m.home_player_8, m.home_player_9, m.home_player_10, m.home_player_11,
        m.away_player_1, m.away_player_2, m.away_player_3, m.away_player_4, m.away_player_5,
        m.away_player_6, m.away_player_7, m.away_player_8, m.away_player_9, m.away_player_10, m.away_player_11
    )
),
players_with_height AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        mp.season,
        mp.player_id,
        pa.height
    FROM match_players mp
    LEFT JOIN Player_Attributes pa ON pa.player_api_id = mp.player_id
    -- Select the latest available Player_Attributes record up to the end of the season
    WHERE pa.date = (
        SELECT MAX(date)
        FROM Player_Attributes pa2
        WHERE pa2.player_api_id = mp.player_id
          AND (
            (mp.season = '2008-2009' AND pa2.date <= '2009-06-30') OR
            (mp.season = '2015-2016' AND pa2.date <= '2016-06-30')
          )
    )
)
SELECT
    t.season_label AS season,
    COUNT(DISTINCT p.player_id) AS player_count,
    ROUND(AVG(p.height), 2) AS avg_height_cm
FROM target_seasons t
LEFT JOIN players_with_height p ON t.season_str = p.season
GROUP BY t.season_label
ORDER BY t.season_label
```

WITH Latest_Player_Attributes AS (
  SELECT
    pa.player_api_id,
    pa.id
  FROM Player_Attributes pa
  INNER JOIN (
    SELECT
      player_api_id,
      MAX(date) AS latest_date
    FROM Player_Attributes
    GROUP BY player_api_id
  ) latest ON
    pa.player_api_id = latest.player_api_id
    AND pa.date = latest.latest_date
  INNER JOIN (
    SELECT
      player_api_id,
      date,
      MAX(id) AS max_id
    FROM Player_Attributes
    GROUP BY player_api_id, date
  ) max_ids ON
    pa.player_api_id = max_ids.player_api_id
    AND pa.date = max_ids.date
    AND pa.id = max_ids.max_id
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS player_count
FROM Player p
INNER JOIN Latest_Player_Attributes lpa
  ON p.player_api_id = lpa.player_api_id
INNER JOIN Player_Attributes pa
  ON pa.id = lpa.id
WHERE p.height > 180
  AND pa.volleys > 70;

    AND season = '2012/2013'
),
snapshot AS (
  SELECT buildUpPlaySpeedClass
  FROM Team_Attributes
  WHERE team_api_id = (SELECT team_api_id FROM team_id)
    AND date <= (SELECT match_date FROM last_match)
  ORDER BY date DESC
  LIMIT 1
)
SELECT buildUpPlaySpeedClass
FROM snapshot;

    pa.date,

  SELECT
    la.player_api_id,

  FROM latest_attrs la

),

  FROM target_players
)

  ROUND(
    ((dr.overall_rating - ar.avg_overall) / ar.avg_overall) * 100.0
    , 2
  ) AS donovan_vs_mean_percentage

WITH first_month AS (
    SELECT MIN(date) as min_date
    FROM account
),
first_month_accounts AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT a.district_id, d.A2 as district_name, d.A3 as inhabitants
    FROM account a
    JOIN district d ON a.district_id = d.district_id
    WHERE a.date >= (SELECT min_date FROM first_month)
      AND a.date < date((SELECT min_date FROM first_month), '+1 month')
),
max_population AS (
    SELECT MAX(CAST(inhabitants AS INTEGER)) as max_inh
    FROM first_month_accounts
)
SELECT district_name, inhabitants
FROM first_month_accounts
WHERE CAST(inhabitants AS INTEGER) = (SELECT max_inh FROM max_population)
ORDER BY district_name;

WITH first_month AS (
    SELECT MIN(open_date) as min_date
    FROM account
),
first_month_accounts AS (
    SELECT a.account_id, c.client_id, d.district_id, d.A2 as district_name, d.A3 as population
    FROM account a
    JOIN disp di ON a.account_id = di.account_id AND di.type = 'OWNER'
    JOIN client c ON di.client_id = c.client_id
    JOIN district d ON c.district_id = d.district_id
    WHERE a.open_date >= (SELECT min_date FROM first_month)

),
districts_with_accounts AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT district_id, district_name, population
    FROM first_month_accounts
),
max_population AS (
    SELECT MAX(population) as max_pop
    FROM districts_with_accounts
)
SELECT district_name, population
FROM districts_with_accounts
WHERE population = (SELECT max_pop FROM max_population)
ORDER BY district_name;
```

  SELECT
    loan.loan_id,
    loan.amount,
    loan.duration,
    loan.date,
    disp.client_id
  FROM loan
  JOIN disp ON loan.account_id = disp.account_id

    AND disp.type = 'OWNER'
),
loan_with_region AS (
  SELECT
    l.loan_id,

  FROM loan_with_region lwr
  JOIN district d ON lwr.district_id = d.district_id
  GROUP BY d.A2
)
SELECT region_name, total_amount
FROM region_totals
WHERE total_amount = (SELECT MAX(total_amount) FROM region_totals)
ORDER BY region_name;

sql:
WITH prachatice_accounts AS (
    SELECT a.account_id, a.district_id AS account_district_id, a.date AS open_date
    FROM account a
    JOIN district d ON a.district_id = d.district_id
    WHERE d.A2 = 'Prachatice'
),
borrowing_accounts AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT l.account_id
    FROM loan l
),
pr_account_loans AS (
    SELECT pa.account_id, pa.open_date
    FROM prachatice_accounts pa
    JOIN borrowing_accounts ba ON pa.account_id = ba.account_id
),
owner_info AS (
    SELECT d.account_id, c.district_id AS client_district_id
    FROM disp d
    JOIN client c ON d.client_id = c.client_id
    WHERE d.type = 'OWNER'
),
account_home_pop AS (
    SELECT pr.account_id,
           pr.open_date,
           oi.client_district_id AS home_district_id,
           dist.A2 AS home_district_name,
           dist.A8 AS home_district_population
    FROM pr_account_loans pr
    JOIN owner_info oi ON pr.account_id = oi.account_id
    JOIN district dist ON oi.client_district_id = dist.district_id
),
total_borrowed AS (
    SELECT l.account_id, SUM(l.amount) AS total_borrowed
    FROM loan l
    GROUP BY l.account_id
),
counterparties AS (
    SELECT
        t.account_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT
            CASE
                WHEN t.type IN ('PRIJEM', 'VYDAJ')
                     AND t.bank IS NOT NULL AND t.bank != ''
                     AND t.account IS NOT NULL
                     AND t.account != t.account_id
                THEN t.bank || '-' || t.account
                ELSE NULL
            END
        ) AS num_outside_counterparties
    FROM trans t
    GROUP BY t.account_id
),
final_table AS (
    SELECT
        ahp.account_id,
        ahp.open_date,
        COALESCE(tb.total_borrowed, 0) AS total_borrowed,
        COALESCE(cp.num_outside_counterparties, 0) AS num_outside_counterparties,
        ahp.home_district_id,
        ahp.home_district_name,
        ahp.home_district_population
    FROM account_home_pop ahp
    LEFT JOIN total_borrowed tb ON ahp.account_id = tb.account_id
    LEFT JOIN counterparties cp ON ahp.account_id = cp.account_id
)
SELECT
    ft.account_id,
    ft.open_date,
    ft.total_borrowed,
    ft.num_outside_counterparties,
    ft.home_district_id,
    ft.home_district_name,
    ft.home_district_population,
    RANK() OVER (
        ORDER BY ft.home_district_population DESC, ft.account_id ASC
    ) AS home_district_population_rank
FROM final_table ft
ORDER BY ft.home_district_population DESC, ft.account_id ASC;

I want to find out whether our borrowing households from larger population centres transact differently from local ones. For every account at the Prachatice branch that has taken at least one loan, please give me: the account number, the account opening date, the total amount ever borrowed, how many outside bank counterparties the account has transacted with over its entire history, the owner's home district, the population of that district, and a rank of these borrowing households by home-district population from largest to smallest. Note that a counterparty means a particular bank account at another institution, identified by that account number, not by the bank code, and only transfers to or from another bank count — handling cash at our own branch does not involve a counterparty. A household's home district is the district its owner client is registered in, which is not necessarily Prachatice. For the ranking: largest population first, ties share the same rank and the next rank after a tie is skipped, and among households whose home districts have the same population, list the smaller account number first.

No follow-up user is available. Give the best supported answer for the question. Return your final answer as exactly one fenced SQL block containing a single read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH query. Exclude intermediate SQL.

```sql
WITH prachatice_accounts AS (
    SELECT a.account_id, a.district_id AS account_district_id, a.open_date
    FROM account a
    JOIN district d ON a.district_id = d.district_id
    WHERE d.name = 'Prachatice'
),
borrowing_accounts AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT l.account_id
    FROM loan l
),
pr_account_loans AS (
    SELECT pa.account_id, pa.open_date
    FROM prachatice_accounts pa
    JOIN borrowing_accounts ba ON pa.account_id = ba.account_id
),
owner_info AS (
    SELECT d.account_id, c.district_id AS client_district_id
    FROM disp d
    JOIN client c ON d.client_id = c.client_id
    WHERE d.type = 'OWNER'
),
account_home_pop AS (
    SELECT pr.account_id,
           pr.open_date,
           oi.client_district_id AS home_district_id,
           dist.name AS home_district_name,
           dist.A2 AS home_district_population
    FROM pr_account_loans pr
    JOIN owner_info oi ON pr.account_id = oi.account_id
    JOIN district dist ON oi.client_district_id = dist.district_id
),
total_borrowed AS (
    SELECT l.account_id, SUM(l.amount) AS total_borrowed
    FROM loan l
    GROUP BY l.account_id
),
counterparties AS (
    SELECT
        t.account_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT
            CASE
                WHEN t.type IN ('PRIJEM', 'VYDAJ')
                     AND t.bank IS NOT NULL AND t.bank != 0
                     AND t.account2 IS NOT NULL
                     AND t.account2 != t.account_id
                THEN printf('%d-%s', t.bank, t.account2)
                ELSE NULL
            END
        ) AS num_outside_counterparties
    FROM trans t
    GROUP BY t.account_id
),
final_table AS (
    SELECT
        ahp.account_id,
        ahp.open_date,
        COALESCE(tb.total_borrowed, 0) AS total_borrowed,
        COALESCE(cp.num_outside_counterparties, 0) AS num_outside_counterparties,
        ahp.home_district_id,
        ahp.home_district_name,
        ahp.home_district_population
    FROM account_home_pop ahp
    LEFT JOIN total_borrowed tb ON ahp.account_id = tb.account_id
    LEFT JOIN counterparties cp ON ahp.account_id = cp.account_id
)
SELECT
    ft.account_id,
    ft.open_date,
    ft.total_borrowed,
    ft.num_outside_counterparties,
    ft.home_district_id,
    ft.home_district_name,
    ft.home_district_population,
    RANK() OVER (
        ORDER BY ft.home_district_population DESC, ft.account_id ASC
    ) AS home_district_population_rank
FROM final_table ft
ORDER BY ft.home_district_population DESC, ft.account_id ASC;

                     AND t.account IS NOT NULL
                     AND t.account != t.account_id

),

  WHERE ab.avg_balance > 1000
),
client_gender AS (
  SELECT
    qa.disp_id,
    qa.account_id,
    qa.client_id,
    cl.gender,
    a.district_id
  FROM qualified_accounts qa

  JOIN account a ON qa.account_id = a.account_id
),
districts_filtered AS (
  SELECT
    cg.gender,
    cg.district_id,
    d.A2 AS district_name,
    d.A8 AS inhabitants,
    d.A11 AS avg_salary,
    d.A10 AS urban_inhabitants,
    CAST(d.A10 AS FLOAT)/d.A8 AS urban_ratio
  FROM client_gender cg
  JOIN district d ON cg.district_id = d.district_id
  WHERE d.A8 > 100000
  GROUP BY cg.gender, cg.district_id
),
stats_per_gender AS (
  SELECT
    gender,
    COUNT(*) AS num_districts,
    ROUND(AVG(avg_salary), 2) AS avg_salary,
    ROUND(AVG(urban_ratio), 2) AS avg_urban_ratio
  FROM districts_filtered
  GROUP BY gender
),
max_inhabitants_per_gender AS (
  SELECT
    gender,
    MAX(inhabitants) AS max_inhabitants
  FROM districts_filtered
  GROUP BY gender
),
top_districts AS (
  SELECT
    d.gender,
    d.district_name,
    d.inhabitants

  JOIN max_inhabitants_per_gender maxd

sql:
WITH gold_card_client_accounts AS (
    SELECT a.account_id
    FROM account a
    JOIN disp d ON a.account_id = d.account_id
    JOIN card c ON d.disp_id = c.disp_id
    WHERE c.type = 'gold'
),
accounts_in_big_cities AS (
    SELECT g.account_id
    FROM gold_card_client_accounts g
    JOIN account a ON g.account_id = a.account_id
    JOIN district di ON a.district_id = di.district_id
    WHERE di.A3 >= 250000
),
filtered_trans AS (
    SELECT t.bank, t.account AS counter_account, t.amount
    FROM trans t
    WHERE t.type = 'VYDAJ' 
      AND t.date BETWEEN 19980101 AND 19981231 
      AND t.account_id IN (SELECT account_id FROM accounts_in_big_cities)
)
SELECT 
    bank, 
    counter_account, 
    COUNT(*) AS num_outgoing_payments, 
    SUM(amount) AS total_amount_paid
FROM filtered_trans
GROUP BY bank, counter_account
HAVING total_amount_paid = (
    SELECT MAX(tt) FROM (
        SELECT SUM(amount) AS tt
        FROM filtered_trans
        GROUP BY bank, counter_account
    )
)
ORDER BY total_amount_paid DESC;

I need a ranking of the recipient bank and counter-account pairs by the total amount paid. If two pairs tie for the largest total, list both. For each pair, give me: the recipient bank code, the recipient counter-account number, the number of outgoing payments, and the total amount paid.

```sql
WITH gold_clients AS (
    SELECT a.account_id, a.district_id
    FROM account a
    JOIN disp d ON a.account_id = d.account_id
    JOIN card c ON d.client_id = c.client_id
    WHERE c.type = 'gold'
),
big_city_accounts AS (
    SELECT gc.account_id
    FROM gold_clients gc
    JOIN district di ON gc.district_id = di.district_id
    WHERE di.A1 >= 250000
),
trans_1998_vydaj AS (
    SELECT t.account_id, t.bank, t.account, t.amount
    FROM trans t
    WHERE t.type = 'VYDAJ'
      AND t.date >= 19980101 AND t.date <= 19981231
)
SELECT
    t.bank AS recipient_bank_code,
    t.account AS recipient_counter_account_number,
    COUNT(*) AS number_of_outgoing_payments,
    SUM(t.amount) AS total_amount_paid
FROM trans_1998_vydaj t
JOIN big_city_accounts bca ON t.account_id = bca.account_id
GROUP BY t.bank, t.account
HAVING SUM(t.amount) = (
    SELECT MAX(total_paid) FROM (
        SELECT SUM(amount) AS total_paid
        FROM trans_1998_vydaj t2
        JOIN big_city_accounts bca2 ON t2.account_id = bca2.account_id
        GROUP BY t2.bank, t2.account
    )
)
ORDER BY total_amount_paid DESC;
```

    SELECT a.account_id
    FROM account a
    JOIN district d ON a.district_id = d.district_id
    WHERE d.A2 = 'Pisek'

    FROM trans t
    WHERE t.account_id IN (SELECT account_id FROM pisek_accounts)

      AND t.k_symbol IS NOT NULL
),
sipo_outgoing AS (

    WHERE k_symbol = 'SIPO'

        (SELECT IFNULL(SUM(amount),1) FROM outgoing_trans_with_purpose)
    , 2
    ) AS sipo_percentage_of_outgoing_with_purpose
;

first_request.user:
I'm planning a regional campaign for female customers who hold a credit card and a loan, and I need a demographic profile per region. For each region, please give me: the region, the average district salary of the districts where these female clients live, and the average 1996 district unemployment rate of those same districts – both averages rounded to 2 decimal places. I also want the name of the most populous district among those districts in each region, so I know where to focus local advertising. A few rules: count only female clients who own the account (disposition type OWNER) and who have at least one credit card and at least one loan on that account. 'Most populous' means the district with the largest number of inhabitants; if two tie, take the one whose name comes first alphabetically. One row per region, and include every region that has at least one such client – nothing else.

No follow-up user is available. Give the best supported answer for the question. Return your final answer as exactly one fenced SQL block containing a single read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH query. Exclude intermediate SQL.

calls.content:
```sql
WITH female_owner_clients AS (
    SELECT
        c.client_id,
        c.birth_number,
        d.account_id,
        a.district_id
    FROM client c
    JOIN disp d ON c.client_id = d.client_id
    JOIN account a ON d.account_id = a.account_id
    WHERE d.type = 'OWNER'
      AND CAST(SUBSTR(LTRIM(PRINTF('%06d', c.birth_number)), 3, 2) AS INTEGER) > 50
),
clients_with_card AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT foc.client_id
    FROM female_owner_clients foc
    JOIN card ca ON foc.disp_id = ca.disp_id
),
clients_with_loan AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT foc.client_id
    FROM female_owner_clients foc
    JOIN loan l ON foc.account_id = l.account_id
),
target_clients AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT foc.account_id, foc.district_id, d.region
    FROM female_owner_clients foc
    JOIN clients_with_card cwc ON foc.client_id = cwc.client_id
    JOIN clients_with_loan cwl ON foc.client_id = cwl.client_id
    JOIN district d ON foc.district_id = d.district_id
),
district_stats AS (
    SELECT
        d.district_id,
        d.region,
        d.name AS district_name,
        d.average_salary,
        d.unemployment_rate_96,
        d.no_of_inhabitants
    FROM district d
),
region_demographics AS (
    SELECT
        tc.region,
        AVG(ds.average_salary) AS avg_salary,
        AVG(ds.unemployment_rate_96) AS avg_unemployment,
        ds.district_id,
        ds.district_name,
        ds.no_of_inhabitants
    FROM target_clients tc
    JOIN district_stats ds ON tc.district_id = ds.district_id
    GROUP BY tc.region, ds.district_id, ds.district_name, ds.no_of_inhabitants
),
most_populous_per_region AS (
    SELECT region, district_name AS most_populous_district, MAX(no_of_inhabitants) AS max_inhabitants
    FROM (
        SELECT
            region,
            district_name,
            no_of_inhabitants,
            RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY no_of_inhabitants DESC, district_name ASC) AS rank
        FROM region_demographics
    )
    WHERE rank = 1
    GROUP BY region
)
SELECT
    rd.region,
    ROUND(AVG(rd.avg_salary), 2) AS avg_district_salary,
    ROUND(AVG(rd.avg_unemployment), 2) AS avg_unemployment_rate_96,
    mpr.most_populous_district
FROM region_demographics rd
JOIN most_populous_per_region mpr ON rd.region = mpr.region
GROUP BY rd.region, mpr.most_populous_district
ORDER BY rd.region;

WITH client_card_districts AS (
    SELECT
        c.type AS card_type,
        cl.district_id,
        d.A2 AS district_name,
        d.A8 AS inhabitants
    FROM card c
    JOIN disp di ON c.disp_id = di.disp_id

    JOIN district d ON cl.district_id = d.district_id
    WHERE c.type IN ('gold', 'classic', 'junior')
),
min_inhabitants_per_type AS (
    SELECT
        card_type,
        MIN(inhabitants) AS min_inhabitants
    FROM client_card_districts
    GROUP BY card_type
)
SELECT
    t.card_type,
    t.district_name,
    t.inhabitants
FROM client_card_districts t
JOIN min_inhabitants_per_type m
  ON t.card_type = m.card_type AND t.inhabitants = m.min_inhabitants
ORDER BY
    t.card_type,
    t.district_name;

WITH
-- 1. Find Litomerice's district_id (A2 is used as district name per schema), then its co-region districts
litomerice_region_districts AS (
  SELECT d2.district_id, d2.A2 AS district_name
  FROM district d1
  JOIN district d2 ON d1.A3 = d2.A3
  WHERE d1.A2 = 'Litomerice'
),
-- 2. Accounts in those districts opened in 1996
accounts_1996 AS (
  SELECT account_id, district_id
  FROM account
  WHERE district_id IN (SELECT district_id FROM litomerice_region_districts)
    AND date >= '1996-01-01' AND date <= '1996-12-31'
),
-- 3. For each account, find the latest transaction id on or before 1996-12-31
last_trans_1996 AS (
  SELECT t.account_id, MAX(t.date) AS last_date
  FROM trans t
  WHERE t.account_id IN (SELECT account_id FROM accounts_1996)
    AND t.date <= '1996-12-31'
  GROUP BY t.account_id
),
final_trans_1996 AS (
  SELECT t1.account_id, t1.trans_id, t1.balance
  FROM trans t1
  JOIN last_trans_1996 lt
    ON t1.account_id = lt.account_id AND t1.date = lt.last_date
  WHERE t1.trans_id = (
    SELECT MAX(t2.trans_id)
    FROM trans t2
    WHERE t2.account_id = t1.account_id AND t2.date = t1.date
  )
),
-- 4. Join accounts to these balances
acct_bal AS (
  SELECT a.account_id, a.district_id, f.balance
  FROM accounts_1996 a
  JOIN final_trans_1996 f ON a.account_id = f.account_id
),
-- 5. Stats per district
district_stats AS (
  SELECT
    d.district_name,
    COUNT(ab.account_id) AS num_accounts_opened_1996,
    ROUND(AVG(ab.balance), 2) AS avg_end_of_1996_balance
  FROM acct_bal ab
  JOIN litomerice_region_districts d ON ab.district_id = d.district_id
  GROUP BY d.district_id, d.district_name
),
-- 6. Region-wide average
region_stats AS (
  SELECT ROUND(AVG(balance), 2) AS region_avg_end_1996_balance
  FROM acct_bal
),
-- 7. Best district by average (alphabetic in case of tie)
top_district AS (
  SELECT district_name, avg_end_of_1996_balance
  FROM district_stats
  WHERE avg_end_of_1996_balance = (SELECT MAX(avg_end_of_1996_balance) FROM district_stats)
  ORDER BY district_name
  LIMIT 1
)
-- Final output as requested
SELECT
  ds.district_name,

  td.district_name AS highest_avg_balance_district,

I'm reviewing how our branches performed in 1996, and I'd like a picture of the money standing in accounts opened during that year, across the region that Litomerice belongs to (the region as given in the district table's region field).

For each district in that region where at least one account was opened in 1996 (openings counted by account creation date within the calendar year 1996), please give me:
- the district name,
- the number of accounts opened in 1996,
- the average end-of-1996 balance of those accounts,
with rows ordered by district name.

Also give me:
- the region-wide average end-of-1996 balance, taken across all those accounts (not as the mean of the district averages),
- the district with the highest average end-of-1996 balance; if two districts tie, name the one that comes first alphabetically.

By end-of-1996 balance I mean the balance after the account's last transaction dated on or before 1996-12-31; transactions dated 1997 or later don't count, and if several transactions fall on that last date, the one with the highest transaction id is the one that matters. Please round all averages to two decimals.

No follow-up user is available. Give the best supported answer for the question. Return your final answer as exactly one fenced SQL block containing a single read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH query. Exclude intermediate SQL.

```sql
WITH
-- 1. Get the region for Litomerice
litomerice_region AS (
  SELECT region
  FROM district
  WHERE district_name = 'Litomerice'
  LIMIT 1
),
-- 2. Districts in Litomerice's region
target_districts AS (
  SELECT A.district_id, A.district_name, A.region
  FROM district A
  JOIN litomerice_region B ON A.region = B.region
),
-- 3. Accounts opened in 1996 in target districts
accounts_1996 AS (
  SELECT a.account_id, a.district_id, strftime('%Y', a.date) AS open_year
  FROM account a
  WHERE a.district_id IN (SELECT district_id FROM target_districts)
    AND a.date >= '1996-01-01' AND a.date <= '1996-12-31'
),
-- 4. For each such account, the last transaction id on or before 1996-12-31
last_tx_1996 AS (
  SELECT
    t.account_id,
    MAX(CASE WHEN t.date <= '1996-12-31'
          THEN (strftime('%s', t.date) || '-' || printf('%09d', t.trans_id))
          ELSE NULL END
    ) AS last_date_txkey
  FROM trans t
  WHERE t.account_id IN (SELECT account_id FROM accounts_1996)
  GROUP BY t.account_id
),
-- 5. Join to get the actual trans_id for the last transaction on/before 1996-12-31
account_final_tx AS (
  SELECT
    a.account_id,
    MAX(t.trans_id) as last_trans_id -- max(trans_id) on the last date
  FROM accounts_1996 a
  LEFT JOIN trans t
    ON a.account_id = t.account_id AND t.date <= '1996-12-31'
  WHERE t.account_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY a.account_id, t.date
  HAVING t.date = (
    SELECT MAX(t2.date)
    FROM trans t2
    WHERE t2.account_id = a.account_id AND t2.date <= '1996-12-31'
  )
),
-- 6. Get each account's end-of-1996 balance
account_1996_balances AS (
  SELECT
    a.account_id,
    a.district_id,
    t.balance
  FROM accounts_1996 a
  JOIN account_final_tx ft
    ON a.account_id = ft.account_id
  JOIN trans t
    ON t.account_id = ft.account_id AND t.trans_id = ft.last_trans_id
),
-- 7. Counts and averages per district
district_stats AS (
  SELECT
    d.district_name,
    COUNT(ab.account_id) AS accounts_opened_1996,
    ROUND(AVG(ab.balance), 2) AS avg_end_1996_balance
  FROM target_districts d
  JOIN account_1996_balances ab ON d.district_id = ab.district_id
  GROUP BY d.district_id, d.district_name
),
-- 8. Region-wide average (single value)
region_avg AS (
  SELECT ROUND(AVG(balance), 2) AS region_avg_1996_balance
  FROM account_1996_balances
),
-- 9. District with max avg balance (using tie-breaker: alpha order)
max_district AS (
  SELECT district_name, avg_end_1996_balance
  FROM district_stats
  WHERE avg_end_1996_balance = (
      SELECT MAX(avg_end_1996_balance) FROM district_stats
  )
  ORDER BY district_name
  LIMIT 1
)
-- Final select
SELECT
  ds.district_name,
  ds.accounts_opened_1996,
  ds.avg_end_1996_balance,
  ra.region_avg_1996_balance,
  md.district_name AS highest_avg_balance_district,
  md.avg_end_1996_balance AS highest_avg_balance
FROM district_stats ds
JOIN region_avg ra ON 1=1
JOIN max_district md ON 1=1
ORDER BY ds.district_name
;

  WHERE d1.A2 = 'Litomerice'
),
-- 2. Accounts in those districts opened in 1996
accounts_1996 AS (
  SELECT account_id, district_id
  FROM account
  WHERE district_id IN (SELECT district_id FROM litomerice_region_districts)
    AND date >= '1996-01-01' AND date <= '1996-12-31'
),
-- 3. For each account, find the latest transaction id on or before 1996-12-31
last_trans_1996 AS (
  SELECT t.account_id, MAX(t.date) AS last_date
  FROM trans t
  WHERE t.account_id IN (SELECT account_id FROM accounts_1996)
    AND t.date <= '1996-12-31'
  GROUP BY t.account_id
),
final_trans_1996 AS (
  SELECT t1.account_id, t1.trans_id, t1.balance
  FROM trans t1
  JOIN last_trans_1996 lt
    ON t1.account_id = lt.account_id AND t1.date = lt.last_date
  WHERE t1.trans_id = (
    SELECT MAX(t2.trans_id)
    FROM trans t2
    WHERE t2.account_id = t1.account_id AND t2.date = t1.date
  )
),
-- 4. Join accounts to these balances
acct_bal AS (
  SELECT a.account_id, a.district_id, f.balance
  FROM accounts_1996 a
  JOIN final_trans_1996 f ON a.account_id = f.account_id
),
-- 5. Stats per district
district_stats AS (
  SELECT
    d.district_name,
    COUNT(ab.account_id) AS num_accounts_opened_1996,
    ROUND(AVG(ab.balance), 2) AS avg_end_of_1996_balance
  FROM acct_bal ab
  JOIN litomerice_region_districts d ON ab.district_id = d.district_id
  GROUP BY d.district_id, d.district_name
),
-- 6. Region-wide average
region_stats AS (
  SELECT ROUND(AVG(balance), 2) AS region_avg_end_1996_balance
  FROM acct_bal
),
-- 7. Best district by average (alphabetic in case of tie)
top_district AS (
  SELECT district_name, avg_end_of_1996_balance
  FROM district_stats
  WHERE avg_end_of_1996_balance = (SELECT MAX(avg_end_of_1996_balance) FROM district_stats)
  ORDER BY district_name
  LIMIT 1
)
-- Final output as requested
SELECT
  ds.district_name,
  ds.num_accounts_opened_1996,
  ds.avg_end_of_1996_balance,
  rs.region_avg_end_1996_balance,
  td.district_name AS highest_avg_balance_district,
  td.avg_end_of_1996_balance AS highest_avg_balance
FROM district_stats ds
CROSS JOIN region_stats rs
CROSS JOIN top_district td
ORDER BY ds.district_name;
```

WITH client_home AS (
    SELECT client_id, district_id AS home_district_id
    FROM client
    WHERE client_id = 3541
),
client_accounts AS (
    SELECT a.account_id, a.district_id, a.frequency, a.date AS date_opened,
           c.home_district_id
    FROM disp d
    JOIN account a ON d.account_id = a.account_id
    JOIN client_home c ON d.client_id = c.client_id
    WHERE d.client_id = 3541
),
account_district AS (
    SELECT ca.account_id, ca.district_id, ca.frequency, ca.date_opened, ca.home_district_id,
           d.A2 AS district_name, d.A3 AS region_name, d.A4 AS num_inhabitants, d.A11 AS avg_salary
    FROM client_accounts ca
    JOIN district d ON ca.district_id = d.district_id
),
loan_info AS (
    SELECT 
        a.account_id,
        COALESCE(l.status, 'none') AS loan_status,
        COALESCE(l.amount, 0) AS loan_amount
    FROM account a
    LEFT JOIN loan l ON a.account_id = l.account_id
),
trans_summary AS (
    SELECT t.account_id,
           COUNT(*) AS num_transactions,
           SUM(CASE WHEN t.type = 'credit' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END) AS total_income,
           SUM(CASE WHEN t.type = 'debit' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END) AS total_expense,
           SUM(CASE WHEN t.type = 'credit' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END) -
           SUM(CASE WHEN t.type = 'debit' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END) AS net_balance
    FROM trans t
    GROUP BY t.account_id
),
region_clients AS (
    SELECT d.A3 AS region_name, COUNT(DISTINCT c.client_id) AS num_clients_in_region
    FROM client c
    JOIN district d ON c.district_id = d.district_id
    GROUP BY d.A3
),
region_pop AS (
    SELECT d.A3 AS region_name, d.A2 AS district_name, d.A4 AS num_inhabitants
    FROM district d
),
region_most_populous AS (
    SELECT rp.region_name, rp.district_name, rp.num_inhabitants
    FROM region_pop rp
    JOIN (
        SELECT region_name, MAX(num_inhabitants) AS max_inhabs
        FROM region_pop
        GROUP BY region_name
    ) mx ON rp.region_name = mx.region_name AND rp.num_inhabitants = mx.max_inhabs
),
pop_rank AS (
    SELECT
        region_name,
        district_name,
        num_inhabitants,
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY region_name ORDER BY CAST(num_inhabitants AS INTEGER) DESC) AS pop_rank
    FROM region_pop
)
SELECT
    ad.account_id,
    ad.date_opened,
    ad.frequency,
    ad.district_name,
    ad.region_name,
    CASE WHEN ad.district_id = ad.home_district_id THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS is_home_district,
    ad.avg_salary,
    li.loan_status,
    li.loan_amount,
    COALESCE(ts.num_transactions, 0) AS num_transactions,
    COALESCE(ts.total_income, 0) AS total_income,
    COALESCE(ts.total_expense, 0) AS total_expense,
    COALESCE(ts.net_balance, 0) AS net_balance,
    rc.num_clients_in_region,
    rmp.district_name AS most_populous_district,
    rmp.num_inhabitants AS most_populous_district_inhabitants,
    pr.pop_rank AS district_population_rank_in_region
FROM account_district ad
LEFT JOIN loan_info li ON ad.account_id = li.account_id
LEFT JOIN trans_summary ts ON ad.account_id = ts.account_id
LEFT JOIN region_clients rc ON ad.region_name = rc.region_name
LEFT JOIN region_most_populous rmp ON ad.region_name = rmp.region_name
LEFT JOIN pop_rank pr ON ad.region_name = pr.region_name AND ad.district_name = pr.district_name
ORDER BY num_transactions DESC, ad.account_id ASC;

    l.loan_id,

  SELECT 
    t.account_id,
    l.loan_id,

sql:
WITH female_clients AS (
    SELECT c.client_id, c.birth_date, c.district_id
    FROM client c
    WHERE c.gender = 'F'
),
approved_loans AS (
    SELECT l.loan_id, l.account_id, l.amount, l.duration, l.payments, l.status, fc.client_id
    FROM loan l
    JOIN disp d ON l.account_id = d.account_id AND d.type = 'OWNER'
    JOIN female_clients fc ON d.client_id = fc.client_id
    WHERE l.status = 'A'
),
largest_loan_amounts AS (
    SELECT amount
    FROM approved_loans
    ORDER BY amount DESC
    LIMIT 3
),
largest_loans AS (
    SELECT al.*
    FROM approved_loans al
    WHERE al.amount IN (SELECT amount FROM largest_loan_amounts)
),
loan_with_acct_branch AS (
    SELECT l.*, a.district_id AS account_district_id
    FROM largest_loans l
    JOIN account a ON l.account_id = a.account_id
),
district_info AS (
    SELECT d.district_id, d.A2 AS district_name, d.A3 AS region, d.A11 AS avg_salary
    FROM district d
),
region_loan_counts AS (
    SELECT di.region, COUNT(l.loan_id) AS region_loan_count
    FROM loan l
    JOIN account a ON l.account_id = a.account_id
    JOIN district d ON a.district_id = d.district_id
    JOIN district_info di ON d.district_id = di.district_id
    GROUP BY di.region
),
region_salary AS (
    SELECT region, ROUND(AVG(avg_salary), 2) AS region_avg_salary
    FROM district_info
    GROUP BY region
),
account_deposits AS (
    SELECT t.account_id,
           COUNT(*) AS transaction_count,
           ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN t.type = 'PRIJEM' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END),2) AS total_deposits
    FROM trans t
    GROUP BY t.account_id
),
client_ages AS (
    SELECT c.client_id,
           CAST(strftime('%Y', '2026-10-09') AS INTEGER) - 
           CAST(strftime('%Y', c.birth_date) AS INTEGER) - 
           CASE WHEN strftime('%m-%d', '2026-10-09') < strftime('%m-%d', c.birth_date) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS completed_age
    FROM client c
)
SELECT
    lwa.client_id,
    lwa.amount AS loan_amount,
    lwa.duration AS duration_months,
    ROUND(lwa.payments*lwa.duration, 2) AS total_payments,
    ROUND(lwa.payments*lwa.duration - lwa.amount, 2) AS interest_paid,
    lwa.status AS loan_status,
    di.district_name,
    di.region,
    ad.transaction_count,
    ad.total_deposits,
    CASE
        WHEN ad.total_deposits > 2 * lwa.amount THEN 'High Income'
        WHEN ad.total_deposits > lwa.amount THEN 'Medium Income'
        ELSE 'Low Income'
    END AS income_category,
    rlc.region_loan_count,
    rs.region_avg_salary,
    ca.completed_age
FROM loan_with_acct_branch lwa
JOIN district_info di ON lwa.account_district_id = di.district_id
LEFT JOIN account_deposits ad ON lwa.account_id = ad.account_id
LEFT JOIN region_loan_counts rlc ON di.region = rlc.region
LEFT JOIN region_salary rs ON di.region = rs.region
LEFT JOIN client_ages ca ON lwa.client_id = ca.client_id
ORDER BY lwa.amount DESC

I need to profile our three largest loans held by female clients. Please report for each of these loans: the client id, loan amount, duration in months, total payments, interest paid, loan status, the district and region of the branch where the loan's account is held, the account's transaction count and total deposits, an income category, the number of loans the bank has granted in that region, the average of the average salaries of that region's districts, and the client's completed age on 2026-10-09. A few notes: the three largest loans are the three highest approved loan amounts, and if amounts tie, include all tied loans. Total payments is the monthly payment times the duration, and interest paid is total payments minus the approved amount; round money figures to two decimals. The income category is High Income if total deposits exceed twice the loan amount, Medium Income if they exceed the loan amount, and Low Income otherwise. Loans in a region counts every loan the bank has granted in that region for all clients, not only female clients. The region's average salary is the average of the average salaries of the districts in that region, rounded to two decimals. For the age, use the completed age on 2026-10-09, subtracting one if the birthday hasn't occurred by that date.

No follow-up user is available. Give the best supported answer for the question. Return your final answer as exactly one fenced SQL block containing a single read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH query. Exclude intermediate SQL.

WITH female_clients AS (
    SELECT c.client_id, c.birth_number
    FROM client c
    WHERE SUBSTR(c.birth_number, 3, 2) >= '50'
),
approved_loans AS (
    SELECT l.loan_id, l.account_id, l.amount, l.duration, l.payments, l.status, fc.client_id
    FROM loan l
    JOIN disp d ON l.account_id = d.account_id AND d.type = 'OWNER'
    JOIN female_clients fc ON d.client_id = fc.client_id
    WHERE l.status = 'A'
),
max_loan_amounts AS (

    FROM approved_loans
    ORDER BY amount DESC

largest_loans AS (
    SELECT al.*
    FROM approved_loans al
    WHERE al.amount IN (SELECT amount FROM max_loan_amounts)
),
loan_with_branch AS (
    SELECT ll.*, a.district_id
    FROM largest_loans ll
    JOIN account a ON ll.account_id = a.account_id
),
district_info AS (
    SELECT d.district_id, d.district_name, d.region, d.avg_salary
    FROM district d
),
region_district_salary AS (
    SELECT region, ROUND(AVG(avg_salary), 2) AS region_avg_salary
    FROM district
    GROUP BY region
),
account_stats AS (
    SELECT t.account_id,
           COUNT(CASE WHEN t.type IN ('PRIJEM', 'DEPOSIT') THEN 1 END) AS total_deposit_count,
           ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN t.type IN ('PRIJEM', 'DEPOSIT') THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END), 2) AS total_deposits,
           COUNT(*) AS total_trans_count
    FROM trans t
    GROUP BY t.account_id
),
loan_region_count AS (

            ELSE CAST(SUBSTR(c.birth_number, 3, 2) AS INTEGER)

    FROM client c
),
client_age_on_date AS (
    SELECT cb.client_id,
        -- Convert year to full year (assuming all births between 1900-1999)
        (CASE WHEN cb.year > '30' THEN '19' || cb.year ELSE '20' || cb.year END) AS full_year,
        cb.month,
        cb.day
    FROM client_birthdates cb
),
client_completed_age AS (
    SELECT ca.client_id,
          (CAST('2026' AS INTEGER) -

    FROM client c
    WHERE c.gender = 'F'
),
approved_loans AS (
    SELECT l.loan_id, l.account_id, l.amount, l.duration, l.payments, l.status, fc.client_id
    FROM loan l
    JOIN disp d ON l.account_id = d.account_id AND d.type = 'OWNER'
    JOIN female_clients fc ON d.client_id = fc.client_id
    WHERE l.status = 'A'
),
largest_loan_amounts AS (
    SELECT amount
    FROM approved_loans
    ORDER BY amount DESC
    LIMIT 3
),
largest_loans AS (
    SELECT al.*
    FROM approved_loans al
    WHERE al.amount IN (SELECT amount FROM largest_loan_amounts)
),
loan_with_acct_branch AS (
    SELECT l.*, a.district_id AS account_district_id
    FROM largest_loans l
    JOIN account a ON l.account_id = a.account_id
),
district_info AS (
    SELECT d.district_id, d.A2 AS district_name, d.A3 AS region, d.A11 AS avg_salary
    FROM district d
),
region_loan_counts AS (
    SELECT di.region, COUNT(l.loan_id) AS region_loan_count
    FROM loan l
    JOIN account a ON l.account_id = a.account_id
    JOIN district d ON a.district_id = d.district_id
    JOIN district_info di ON d.district_id = di.district_id
    GROUP BY di.region
),
region_salary AS (
    SELECT region, ROUND(AVG(avg_salary), 2) AS region_avg_salary
    FROM district_info
    GROUP BY region
),
account_deposits AS (
    SELECT t.account_id,
           COUNT(*) AS transaction_count,
           ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN t.type = 'PRIJEM' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END),2) AS total_deposits
    FROM trans t
    GROUP BY t.account_id
),

    SELECT c.client_id,
           CAST(strftime('%Y', '2026-10-09') AS INTEGER) - 
           CAST(strftime('%Y', c.birth_date) AS INTEGER) - 
           CASE WHEN strftime('%m-%d', '2026-10-09') < strftime('%m-%d', c.birth_date) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS completed_age
    FROM client c
)

    lwa.client_id,

JOIN district_info di ON lwa.account_district_id = di.district_id

LEFT JOIN region_loan_counts rlc ON di.region = rlc.region
LEFT JOIN region_salary rs ON di.region = rs.region
LEFT JOIN client_ages ca ON lwa.client_id = ca.client_id
ORDER BY lwa.amount DESC

WITH gold_accounts AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT a.account_id, d.A2 AS district_name, d.A3 AS region
    FROM account a
    JOIN district d ON a.district_id = d.district_id
    JOIN disp di ON a.account_id = di.account_id
    JOIN card c ON di.disp_id = c.disp_id
    WHERE c.type = 'gold'
),
trans_summ AS (
    SELECT
        t.account_id,
        SUM(CASE WHEN t.type = 'credit' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END) AS total_received,
        SUM(CASE WHEN t.type = 'debit' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END) AS total_withdrawn,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t.bank IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(t.bank) <> '' THEN t.bank || ':' || IFNULL(t.account,'') ELSE NULL END) AS external_counterparties
    FROM trans t
    GROUP BY t.account_id
),
loan_counts AS (
    SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS num_loans
    FROM loan
    GROUP BY account_id
),
summary AS (
    SELECT
        ga.account_id,
        ga.district_name,
        ga.region,
        COALESCE(ts.total_received, 0) AS total_received,
        COALESCE(ts.total_withdrawn, 0) AS total_withdrawn,
        COALESCE(lc.num_loans, 0) AS num_loans,
        COALESCE(ts.external_counterparties, 0) AS external_counterparties
    FROM gold_accounts ga
    LEFT JOIN trans_summ ts ON ga.account_id = ts.account_id
    LEFT JOIN loan_counts lc ON ga.account_id = lc.account_id
)
SELECT
    account_id,
    district_name,
    region,
    total_received,
    total_withdrawn,
    num_loans,
    external_counterparties,

WITH tabor_branch AS (
    SELECT a.account_id, a.date AS account_open_date
    FROM account a
    JOIN district d ON a.district_id = d.district_id
    WHERE d.A2 = 'Tabor'
),
owners AS (
    SELECT disp.account_id, c.gender, c.birth_date
    FROM disp
    JOIN client c ON disp.client_id = c.client_id
    WHERE disp.type = 'OWNER'
),
owner_ages AS (
    SELECT account_id, gender, (
        CAST(strftime('%Y', '1996-12-31') AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', birth_date) AS INTEGER)
        - CASE WHEN strftime('%m-%d', birth_date) > '12-31' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
    ) AS age_on_1996_12_31
    FROM owners
),
cards_ct AS (
    SELECT disp.account_id, COUNT(*) AS num_cards
    FROM card
    JOIN disp ON card.disp_id = disp.disp_id
    WHERE card.issued <= '1996-12-31'
    GROUP BY disp.account_id
),
loans_ct AS (
    SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS num_loans
    FROM loan
    WHERE date <= '1996-12-31'
    GROUP BY account_id
),
loans_status AS (
    SELECT account_id,
           MAX(CASE WHEN status = 'B' THEN 3 WHEN status IN ('C','D') THEN 2 WHEN status = 'A' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS status_rank
    FROM loan
    WHERE date <= '1996-12-31'
    GROUP BY account_id
),
loan_labels AS (
    SELECT tabor.account_id,
        CASE 
          WHEN IFNULL(loans_ct.num_loans,0) = 0 THEN 'no loan'
          WHEN IFNULL(loans_status.status_rank,0) = 3 THEN 'defaulted'
          WHEN IFNULL(loans_status.status_rank,0) = 2 THEN 'repaying'
          ELSE 'paid off' END AS loan_standing
    FROM tabor_branch tabor
    LEFT JOIN loans_ct ON tabor.account_id = loans_ct.account_id
    LEFT JOIN loans_status ON tabor.account_id = loans_status.account_id
),
trans_97 AS (
    SELECT account_id,
      COUNT(*) as num_transactions,
      SUM(CASE WHEN type = 'credit' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS money_in,
      SUM(CASE WHEN type IN ('debit','withdrawal') THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS money_out
    FROM trans
    WHERE date BETWEEN '1997-01-01' AND '1997-12-31'
    GROUP BY account_id
),
balances_97 AS (
    SELECT account_id, MAX(balance) AS peak_balance
    FROM trans
    WHERE date BETWEEN '1997-01-01' AND '1997-12-31'
    GROUP BY account_id
),
ranked_peaks AS (
  SELECT account_id, IFNULL(peak_balance,0) as peak_balance,
         (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT IFNULL(peak_balance,0)) FROM balances_97 b2 WHERE IFNULL(b2.peak_balance,0) > IFNULL(balances_97.peak_balance,0)) + 1 AS peak_balance_rank
  FROM tabor_branch
  LEFT JOIN balances_97 USING(account_id)
)
SELECT 
    tabor.account_id,
    tabor.account_open_date,
    owner_ages.gender,
    owner_ages.age_on_1996_12_31 AS owner_age_on_1996_12_31,
    IFNULL(cards_ct.num_cards,0) AS num_cards_issued_by_1996,
    IFNULL(loans_ct.num_loans,0) AS num_loans_approved_by_1996,
    loan_labels.loan_standing AS loan_standing_label,
    IFNULL(trans_97.num_transactions,0) AS num_transactions_1997,
    IFNULL(trans_97.money_in,0) AS total_money_in_1997,
    IFNULL(trans_97.money_out,0) AS total_money_out_1997,
    ranked_peaks.peak_balance,
    ranked_peaks.peak_balance_rank
FROM tabor_branch tabor
JOIN owner_ages ON tabor.account_id = owner_ages.account_id
LEFT JOIN cards_ct ON tabor.account_id = cards_ct.account_id
LEFT JOIN loans_ct ON tabor.account_id = loans_ct.account_id
LEFT JOIN loan_labels ON tabor.account_id = loan_labels.account_id
LEFT JOIN trans_97 ON tabor.account_id = trans_97.account_id
JOIN ranked_peaks ON tabor.account_id = ranked_peaks.account_id
ORDER BY ranked_peaks.peak_balance_rank ASC, tabor.account_id ASC;

first_request.user:
I'm preparing our branch's annual customer review. For every account held at the Tabor branch as of 31 December 1996, I need a one-row profile per account, ordered among tied ranks by ascending account id, showing: the account id; the date the account was opened; the owner's gender and their age at 31 December 1996 in whole completed years; the number of credit cards issued to the account by 31 December 1996 (0 if none); the number of loans approved to the account by 31 December 1996 (0 if none); a loan standing label; the number of transactions on the account during 1997; the total money into the account during 1997; the total money out of the account during 1997; the peak balance reached on the account during 1997 (0 if none); and the account's rank by 1997 peak balance, highest first, with ties sharing a rank and the next rank skipped (e.g. 1, 1, 3). All 'as of' figures are taken at 31 December 1996; activity figures cover the calendar year 1997. A card or loan counts as held if it was issued or approved on or before 31 December 1996. The loan standing label is: 'no loan' if the account had no loans approved by 31 December 1996; otherwise 'defaulted' if any of its loans has repayment status B; otherwise 'repaying' if any has status C or D; otherwise 'paid off'. Money in is the sum of credit transaction amounts; money out is the sum of debit and cash-withdrawal transaction amounts. The account owner is the person with the 'OWNER' disposition on the account; other dispositions are just additional users. Nothing beyond these fields, please.

No follow-up user is available. Give the best supported answer for the question. Return your final answer as exactly one fenced SQL block containing a single read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH query. Exclude intermediate SQL.
